chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For the Muslim upon his brother, from the rights, is that he greets him when he meets him, and visits him when he is sick, and advises him when he is absent, and says the Name of Allah when he sneezes, saying: "The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, there is no associate for Him," and he says to him: "May Allah have mercy on you." So he answers him, saying to him: "May Allah guide you and rectify your affairs." And he answers him when he invites him, and follows him (his funeral) when he dies.'

key_terms.يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ: May Allah guide you (response to sneezing)
key_terms.يُسَمِّتَهُ: Says the Name of Allah (upon sneezing)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights of a Muslim upon his brother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the comprehensive social contract between Muslims, framing these etiquette rules as binding rights (huquq) that strengthen communal bonds. The specific response to sneezing, invoking Allah as 'Lord of the Worlds' without partner, reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating monotheistic affirmation into daily interactions, while the sequence of rights—from greeting to funeral attendance—illustrates the holistic care expected in the Muslim community.
